# WDI Figure Programming Intern, Spring 2027 — Walt Disney Imagineering

---

**Job ID:** 10159712
**Date Posted:** Aug 31, 2026
**Date Applied:** Sep 3, 2026
**Salary Range:** $26.50/hr (undergraduate) or $27.50/hr (graduate level) — Glendale, CA or Orlando, FL

---

## Job Summary

A Spring 2027 internship (approximately January 2027 – June 2027) on WDI Animation's Show Programming team, fully on-site in Glendale, CA or Celebration, FL. The role sits within the group that "creates the illusion of life" for Disney's Audio-Animatronics figures — prototypical design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly, figure finishing, installation, show programming, and animation.

---

## What You'll Do

- Work closely with other Show Programmers to operate and maintain Animation & Show Programming system's specialized hardware and software tools.
- Assist in creating, debugging, and coordinating Audio-Animatronic figures' digital assets (character sheets, animation data, rigs, ride paths, shots, and/or models).
- Build and review digital animation rigs.
- Provide pipeline and animation process support and asset integration to the Show Animators for Audio-Animatronics programming.
- Partner with the creative team and show programming team to program special effects, audio, animated props, and show action equipment.
- Organize, secure, and maintain show data created by the Animators and Show Programmers.
- Provide technical support for computer graphic animation programs (such as Maya and MotionBuilder).
- Assist in developing or maintaining show programming tools; learn proprietary software packages.

### Required Qualifications
- Familiarity with creating and maintaining rigs for CG character animation
- Ability to function in a dynamic work environment, managing multiple project tasks
- Basic knowledge of robotic animation, control systems, and mechanical systems
- Ability to provide basic technical support for computer graphic animation applications
- Ability to work with limited supervision while integrating input from many individuals as a team member
- High tolerance for change and changing requirements
- Preferred: familiarity with Maya, MotionBuilder, ZBrush, MS Excel, Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, Premiere, After Effects, SolidWorks, Tait Navigator, Shotgun, Rhino, Unreal/Unity; scripting knowledge in Python, Mel, C, or C++; experience with game engines
- A portfolio link on the resume is required for full consideration

### Education
Currently enrolled as a Junior or higher at an accredited college/university, majoring in traditional animation, computer animation, industrial automation control programming, or a related field. Eligibility requires being enrolled and taking at least one class at time of application (or currently in a Disney College Program/Internship), age 18+, unrestricted work authorization, and not having completed a full year of continuous employment on a prior Disney internship or program.

### Benefits
Select benefits may be provided as part of the compensation package (medical, financial, and/or other), dependent on level and position offered.

---

## How I Match Up

### At Application — Sep 3, 2026

- **The disqualifying gap is eligibility, not skill:** this posting requires current enrollment as a Junior or higher at an accredited college/university, taking at least one class at the time of application. The BS in Electro-Mechanical Engineering from Penn State was completed in December 2024 — there is no current enrollment on record, which is a hard eligibility requirement for this internship program, not a soft preference.
- **Partial overlap on the general engineering side:** "basic knowledge of robotic animation, control systems, and mechanical systems" overlaps with real experience — Allen Bradley PLCs, automation equipment development, LabVIEW-based control/data-acquisition systems, and extensive mechanical/electrical design work across Filament Innovations/Proteor's ICARUS, POSEIDON, and Kraken platforms.
- **Genuine skill gaps on the animation-specific stack:** no evidence of Maya, MotionBuilder, ZBrush, or CG character-rig work — the core preferred/required tools for this specific role — and no Audio-Animatronics or show-programming experience on record. SolidWorks and Python are on record and both appear in the posting's preferred list, but the required qualifications center on animation pipeline tools this profile doesn't currently show.
- Given the enrollment requirement, the application was marked not in consideration.

### Now — Sep 4, 2026

No material change — this was evaluated one day after application, and the disqualifying factor (not currently enrolled in college) hasn't changed.

---

## About the Company

This posting sits within WDI Animation, part of Walt Disney Imagineering's Show Systems organization, responsible for the design, engineering, and show programming of Audio-Animatronics figures across Disney's theme parks, resorts, attractions, and cruise ships.
